entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE). The review states the limit of treatment in this disease class: seizures and motor signs respond better than cognition.
entries.snippet: Available treatments are more effective on epileptic manifestations and motor symptoms, whereas benefits on cognitive outcome are generally poor.[1,2]

entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE. What a pyridoxine trial can and cannot say: a response is a diagnostic step, and the absence of a response does not exclude the disease; the review therefore licenses no inference from a negative trial.
entries.snippet: This response has no diagnostic value and if it is lacking, the diagnosis cannot be excluded.[5]

entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE. The defining readout of cerebral folate deficiency is a CSF measurement without peripheral depletion, which a blood folate level would not show; this is the readout class a WWOX-folate question would need, and no WWOX report contains it.
entries.snippet: The main biochemical marker of a cerebral folate deficiency is represented by an extremely low 5-methyltetrahydrofolate concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid without evidences of peripheral folate depletion.[20,21]

entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE. Metabolic derangement in the neonatal PNPO form includes acidosis, hyperlactataemia and hypoglycaemia with anaemia: shows that a cofactor-pathway DEE can carry glucose and lactate abnormalities, a class-level comparison for hypoglycaemia in the Wwox-null mouse and not a WWOX finding.
entries.snippet: signs of metabolic derangement (including metabolic acidosis, hyperlactacidemia, hypoglycemia), anemia, and gastrointestinal symptoms

entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE. Ketogenic diet is the gold-standard treatment of GLUT1 deficiency because it supplies an alternative brain fuel; the effect on cognition is not established. It supports the class statement that a diet can substitute a blocked glucose supply, nothing about WWOX.
entries.snippet: Ketogenic diet remains to be the gold standard for treatment of GLUT1 deficiency because it represents an alternative source of energy for the brain.[34]

entries.proposition: Table 1 (image, opened): the proposed checklist. First-level tests: blood count, blood gases and electrolytes, glucose, liver function, ammonia, uric acid, thyroid function; newborns and infants get therapeutic trials of pyridoxine, pyridoxal phosphate or folinic acid; epilepsy with movement disorder gets lactate, pyruvate, guanidinoacetate, urinary creatine/creatinine, pterins, CSF glucose ratio; multi-organ patients get lactate, acylcarnitines, amino acids, folates, homocysteine; second and third level tests are named. It lists the cofactor work-up a WWOX-related DEE case would be screened against, as a class checklist.
